You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 12e1e7af1a55b9f911025365af4c689b3933c22a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert+renesas@glider.be>
Date: Wed, 20 Feb 2019 13:50:59 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] vfs: Make __vfs_write() static

__vfs_write() was unexported, and removed from <linux/fs.h>, but
forgotten to be made static.

Fixes: eb031849d52e61d2 ("fs: unexport __vfs_read/__vfs_write")
Signed-off-by: Geert Uytterhoeven <geert+renesas@glider.be>
Signed-off-by: Al Viro <viro@zeniv.linux.org.uk>
---
 fs/read_write.c | 4 ++--
 1 file changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/read_write.c b/fs/read_write.c
index 27b69b85d49f..d83003d856a0 100644
--- a/fs/read_write.c
+++ b/fs/read_write.c
@@ -478,8 +478,8 @@ static ssize_t new_sync_write(struct file *filp, const char __user *buf, size_t
 	return ret;
 }
 
-ssize_t __vfs_write(struct file *file, const char __user *p, size_t count,
-		    loff_t *pos)
+static ssize_t __vfs_write(struct file *file, const char __user *p,
+			   size_t count, loff_t *pos)
 {
 	if (file->f_op->write)
 		return file->f_op->write(file, p, count, pos);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The function `__vfs_write()` was unexported and removed from the public header `<linux/fs.h>`, but it was not made static in the source file `fs/read_write.c`, leading to potential linkage issues or unintended access from other parts of the codebase. Making it static ensures that the function is only accessible within the file it is defined, preventing external calls and maintaining encapsulation.

Root cause:
The function `__vfs_write()` was unexported and removed from the public header `<linux/fs.h>`, but it was not made static in the source file `fs/read_write.c`, leading to potential linkage issues or unintended access from other parts of the codebase. Making it static ensures that the function is only accessible within the file it is defined, preventing external calls and maintaining encapsulation.
